context.analysis:
## Overview
[System: Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System] screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud before approval and provides case management for analyst reviews.

## Key Elements
• Merchant / Payment Gateway
• Fraud Analyst
• Risk & Compliance Officer
• Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (Target)
• Payment Processing Core / Acquirer
• Identity Provider (IdP)
• AWS Audit & Compliance Store
• Notification / Alerting Service
• AWS CloudWatch / Observability Platform
• CI/CD & Model Registry Pipeline

## Relationships
• Merchant / Payment Gateway -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System via gRPC / HTTPS
• Fraud Analyst -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
• Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System -> AWS Audit & Compliance Store via HTTPS / S3 API
• Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System -> Notification / Alerting Service via API
• Payment Processing Core -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System via mTLS

## Technology Stack
• AWS (eu-west-1): Chosen for localized managed infrastructure within budget and team capacity
• gRPC: Enables low-latency communication for sub-50ms P99 responses
• OAuth2/OIDC & IdP: Secures authentication, RBAC, and hardware-backed MFA for analysts
• AWS S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode): Ensures 7-year tamper-evident WORM audit retention
• AWS CloudWatch & AWS X-Ray: Provides centralized observability and distributed tracing

## Rationale
This architecture balances PCI-DSS compliance, strict sub-50ms performance, and a 7-year tamper-evident audit trail. It remains operable by a 3-engineer team within a 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System designed to screen card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and provide case management for fraud analysts. Its core purpose is to block fraudulent transactions while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a sub-50ms P99 latency.]

## Key Elements
- Decision API Container [container]
- Scoring Engine Container [container]
- Case Management Portal Container [container]
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL [container]
- CI/CD & Model Registry Pipeline [externalSystem, context]
- Identity Provider (IdP) [externalSystem, context]
- AWS Audit & Compliance Store [externalSystem, context]

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway -> Decision API Container (gRPC / HTTPS)
- Decision API Container -> Scoring Engine Container (Internal VPC gRPC / mTLS)
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management Portal Container (HTTPS (TLS 1.3))
- Case Management Portal Container -> Identity Provider (IdP) (OIDC / OAuth2)
- Scoring Engine Container -> AWS Audit & Compliance Store (HTTPS / S3 API)

## Technology Stack
- AWS Fargate [infrastructure]: Standardizes compute for Decision and Scoring containers to eliminate Lambda cold starts and meet latency SLAs.
- Go [language]: Powers the Decision API for high-performance and low-latency authorization checks.
- Python / FastAPI [language / framework]: Powers the Scoring Engine for ML model inference.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL [database]: Stores transactional case data with read replicas.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock [storage]: Implements WORM storage for the 7-year tamper-evident audit requirement.

## Rationale
[Standardizing on AWS Fargate ensures predictable sub-50ms P99 latency while avoiding Kubernetes complexity for a three-engineer team. Edge tokenization and strict VPC isolation satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and robust auditability within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]

Decision API Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages analyst reviews. It ensures high performance and PCI-DSS compliance under strict latency constraints.

## Key Elements
- Decision API Container (Go, AWS Fargate)
- Scoring Engine Container (Python, FastAPI, AWS Fargate)
- Case Management Portal Container (AWS Fargate)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL)
- API Handler Component (Go)
- Circuit Breaker & Fallback Manager (Go)
- Audit Dispatcher Component (Go)

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway -> Decision API Container [gRPC / HTTPS]

- AWS Fargate: Provides container orchestration within a €25,000 monthly budget.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Go and Fargate to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS. Robust encryption, tokenization, and audit trails ensure full compliance with PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit requirements.

Scoring Engine Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud prior to approval and provides a case management portal for fraud analysts. It is built to maintain PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 50 ms P99 latency threshold under high transaction volumes.

## Key Elements
- Decision API Container (Go, AWS Fargate)
- Scoring Engine Container (Python, FastAPI, AWS Fargate)
- Case Management Portal Container (AWS Fargate)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
- Inference API Controller (Python, FastAPI)
- Model Registry Sync Agent (Python)
- Model Execution Engine (Python, ONNX Runtime / Triton Inference Server)
- Feature Extraction Component (Python)
- Explanation Generation Component (Python)
- AWS Audit & Compliance Store
- CI/CD & Model Registry Pipeline

## Relationships
- Decision API Container -> Scoring Engine Container [Internal VPC gRPC / mTLS]
- Inference API Controller -> Feature Extraction Component [In-Memory Function Call]
- Inference API Controller -> Model Execution Engine [In-Memory Function Call / ONNX Runtime C-API]
- Model Execution Engine -> Explanation Generation Component [In-Memory Function Call]
- Model Registry Sync Agent -> CI/CD & Model Registry Pipeline [HTTPS / S3 API]
- Scoring Engine Container -> AWS Audit & Compliance Store [HTTPS / S3 API]

## Technology Stack
- AWS Fargate with Graviton2 (ARM64): Optimizes price-performance for containerized workloads within budget.
- Python, FastAPI, and ONNX Runtime / Triton Inference Server: Ensures high-throughput, low-latency machine learning model inference.
- Go: Powers the Decision API Container for high-performance authorization handling.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Provides reliable transactional storage for case management.
- AWS KMS: Secures private keys for cryptographic audit signing.

## Rationale
This architecture uses ONNX Runtime on ARM64 AWS Fargate to meet the stringent 50 ms P99 latency requirement at high throughput. Asynchronous explanation offloading and strict memory zeroization ensure compliance with PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year tamper-evident audit mandates.

Case Management Portal Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Portal Container provides a secure, high-performance web interface for fraud analysts to review flagged transactions, execute bulk decisions, and inspect model explainability. It operates as part of the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System within strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance constraints.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (person)
- Case Management Portal Container (container, AWS Fargate)
- UI Presentation Component (component, React/TypeScript, Nginx)
- Case Management API Component (component, Node.js/TypeScript)
- Audit Logging Component (component)
- Identity Provider (IdP) (externalSystem)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (container)
- AWS Audit & Compliance Store (externalSystem)
- AWS CloudWatch / Observability Platform (externalSystem)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> UI Presentation Component: HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- UI Presentation Component -> Case Management API Component: HTTPS (JSON/REST)
- Case Management API Component -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: SQL / TLS
- Case Management API Component -> AWS Audit & Compliance Store: HTTPS / S3 API
- Case Management API Component -> AWS CloudWatch / Observability Platform: HTTPS / AWS SDK
- UI Presentation Component -> Identity Provider (IdP): OIDC / OAuth2

## Technology Stack
- AWS Fargate: Chosen for container orchestration to fit the 3-person team and 25,000 EUR monthly budget without Kubernetes overhead.
- React/TypeScript & Nginx: Powers the UI Presentation Component with strict CSP headers and client-side card data masking.
- Node.js/TypeScript: Powers the Case Management API Component for efficient asynchronous case workflow handling.
- AWS KMS (AES-256): Secures local disk buffers and encrypted storage for tamper-evident compliance audit trails.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Stores transactional case data with read replicas.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages managed serverless containers on AWS to maintain a fixed low operational footprint suited for a three-engineer team. It embeds robust cryptographic audit logging and strict data masking to satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability mandates without exceeding budget constraints.

Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
This system screens real-time card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and provides case management tools for fraud analysts. It ensures sub-50ms decision latency while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System
- Fraud Analyst
- Risk & Compliance Officer
- Merchant / Payment Gateway
- Payment Processing Core / Acquirer
- Identity Provider (IdP)
- AWS Audit & Compliance Store
- Notification / Alerting Service
- AWS CloudWatch / Observability Platform
- CI/CD & Model Registry Pipeline
- Decision API Container (Go, AWS Fargate)
- Scoring Engine Container (Python, FastAPI, AWS Fargate)
- Case Management Portal Container (AWS Fargate)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL)

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (gRPC / HTTPS)
- Fraud Analyst -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (HTTPS (TLS 1.3))
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System -> AWS Audit & Compliance Store (HTTPS / S3 API)
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System -> Notification / Alerting Service (API)
- Payment Processing Core / Acquirer -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (mTLS)
- Merchant / Payment Gateway -> Decision API Container (gRPC / HTTPS)
- Decision API Container -> Scoring Engine Container (Internal VPC gRPC / mTLS)
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management Portal Container (HTTPS (TLS 1.3))
- Case Management Portal Container -> Identity Provider (IdP) (OIDC / OAuth2)
- Scoring Engine Container -> AWS Audit & Compliance Store (HTTPS / S3 API)

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for the Decision API Container to ensure high-performance and low-latency authorization checks.
- Python & FastAPI: Powers the Scoring Engine Container for rapid ML model inference.
- AWS Fargate: Runs all containers serverlessly to stay within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget and minimize operational overhead for a 3-engineer team.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Stores transactional case data, utilizing read replicas and RDS Proxy to maintain the P99 <50ms latency SLA.
- pgAudit: Native PostgreSQL extension utilized for mandatory compliance logging.

## Rationale
The serverless Fargate and managed Aurora PostgreSQL architecture minimizes operational overhead for a three-engineer team while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 security. Microsecond-optimized Go and Python runtimes combined with RDS Proxy guarantee sub-50ms decision latency at 3,000 TPS within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
